Mathematical Genealogy

Close relations of the Top 100, by proximity level

Every PhD mathematician has an advisor, and every advisor has an advisor. The Mathematics Genealogy Project catalogs this lineage. We use it to surface close relations: researchers who are not in the algorithmic Top 100 by publication count, but who sit in its immediate orbit through advisor-student relationships.

How proximity levels work

We build one graph from the advisor and descendant trees of all Top 100 researchers (the seeds), then look at everyone who is not already in the directory. Each outsider is graded by how many distinct Top 100 researchers they are directly connected to as advisor or student:

  • Level 1: directly connected to three or more Top 100 researchers. The most central figures. (1 researcher.)
  • Level 2: directly connected to exactly two. (11 researchers.)
  • Level 3: directly connected to one. This is the broad one-hop neighbourhood (several hundred people), so it is not listed here.

This page shows the complete Level 1 and Level 2 groups. People already in the directory (Top 100, next 100, or In Memoriam) and deceased mathematicians are excluded, the latter belong on the In Memoriam page. Click any name for a detail page.

Notes

  • Peter Sarnak (Stanford University, 1980): A leading analytic number theorist at Princeton and the Institute for Advanced Study. His advisor-student network reaches three Top 100 researchers, the strongest single genealogy tie to the directory.
  • Olli Järviniemi (Turun yliopisto, 2023): A young Finnish number theorist (PhD Turku 2023), connected through close advisor-student ties to Kaisa Matomäki and the Turku school.
  • Mattia Cafferata (Università degli Studi di Ferrara, 2019): An Italian number theorist (PhD Ferrara 2019) in the analytic prime-number tradition, linked to the directory through shared advisors.
  • Stefan Neumann (Universität Stuttgart, 2006): A number theorist (PhD Stuttgart 2006) tied to the German analytic number theory lineage that runs through the directory.
  • Kam Hung Yau (University of New South Wales, 2020): A number theorist (PhD UNSW 2020) working on exponential sums, connected to the Sydney analytic number theory group.
  • Christian Bagshaw (University of New South Wales, 2025): A recent number theory PhD (UNSW 2025), connected to the directory through the Sydney analytic number theory school.
  • Taiyu Li (Shandong University, 2012): A number theorist (PhD Shandong 2012) from the Shandong analytic number theory school that anchors much of the Chinese Goldbach work.
  • Sofia Lindqvist (University of Oxford, 2019): A number theorist (PhD Oxford 2019) working on additive combinatorics and the distribution of primes, reaching the directory through the Oxford lineage.
  • Timothy Trudgian (University of Oxford, 2010): An analytic number theorist (PhD Oxford 2010) known for explicit estimates related to the zeros of the zeta function, tied to the Oxford and Australian schools.
  • Douglas Woodall (University of Nottingham, 1969): A combinatorialist and number theorist (PhD Nottingham 1969) connected to the directory through advisor-student ties.
  • Dorian Goldfeld (Columbia University, 1969): An analytic number theorist at Columbia (PhD 1969), known for work on L-functions and the Gauss class number problem, linked to the directory's lineage.
  • Michael Filaseta (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, 1984): A number theorist (PhD Illinois 1984) working on polynomials and primes, connected through shared advisors with the directory.
